rationale:
Two 090 diagnosis runs on bugs_open/029 have now stalled at UNVERIFIABLE for the same avoidable reason: the diagnosis evidence bundle carries no schema for awaited_requests, so the loop cannot write a row query against the one table that holds the evidence. The second run (corr d8af5f78-98bd-46fa-85b0-2a6899617db8, 2026-08-19) said so in its own data_request: 'awaited_requests is not in the bundle's schema listing; its columns must be confirmed before a targeted row query can be written to check for the stuck spawn_handler awaited request.' It had already identified the right table and the right code path (its RuntimeSite reads 'build-dispatch-loop orchestration - awaited_requests / response-consumer goroutine'), so this is purely a harness gap, not a bad symptom.

This is run 074beb8a's failure one table over. That run died because orchestration_states was absent from the Schema section, guessed a column name, got SQLSTATE 42703 and stopped; the remedy was schemaAlwaysTables, and the fix worked. awaited_requests falls outside BOTH filters that populate the section: it does not match the relevance include (site%|page%|content%|flow%) and no SELECT in diagnose_load_runtime names it, which is the rule the always-list is derived from. So it is invisible by construction and will stay invisible until named.

Why this table specifically, rather than widening the include: awaited_requests is the step-level twin of orchestration_states, holding the per-request rows (retry_version, status, sent_at, timeout_at, processed_at, processing_started_at) that every orchestration-hang question is actually answered from. It also RETAINS SEVEN DAYS where orchestration_states retains about twenty-six hours - measured 2026-08-19 - so it is routinely the only table that still holds the incident. On bugs_open/029 the full 20-instance wedge population is reconstructible from it after orchestration_states has lost every row.

The change is one entry in a list plus one test assertion. It ships no new mechanism, no new key and no new authority: it makes an existing, already-reviewed mechanism (the always-list) cover one more table.

plan.summary: Add awaited_requests to schemaAlwaysTables in diagnose_load_runtime, so the diagnosis bundle's Schema section always describes its columns. State the widened derivation rule in the comment (the list is now 'tables this action renders rows from' PLUS 'tables a diagnosis cannot avoid addressing'), because no SELECT in that file names awaited_requests and a future reader would otherwise delete it as unused. Guard that deletion with its own assertion in TestSchemaAlwaysTablesIsDeterministic, mirroring the existing orchestration_states assertion which exists for exactly this reason.

edits.rationale: One entry, sorted into place. The existing derivation test asserts only queried-implies-listed, so adding a table breaks nothing; the comment is amended in the same edit so the list's rule is not silently falsified by its own contents.

The coverage test derives the list from SELECTs in the source and therefore CANNOT see why awaited_requests belongs; it would stay green if the entry were removed as apparently-unused. This assertion is the only thing preventing a silent regression, and it names the two 090 runs so the reason survives. Proven able to fail: removing the entry fails this test with the intended message; restoring it passes.
